messages.author: 1557f895f706963e
messages.subject: INLA versioning
parts:
For the sake of reproducibility in research, I would like to refer readers/users to a specific version of INLA even after that version becomes outdated. I noticed that only the most recent few versions are posted, and I'm worried that the current version will vanish within a few months of my next paper.

Also, I don't understand INLA's versioning system. What does "Version 0.0-1432754561" mean? No chronology is apparent.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA versioning
parts:
Currently, the safest (and long-term stable) method to identify a specific version for the purpose of being able to recreate it at a later data is to refer to the mercurial ID of the revision used to build the package; that can be used to download any specific version of the source code (and, with some work, build a package from it, see e.g. build-user/linux/Makefile that has an option to download and build a specific version identified by a tagged revision jss2014). See the output of the 
  inla.version()
command, where the line "INLA hgid" gives the necessary revision identifier.
Sometimes the following line, "INLA-program hgid" is different. This should almost always mean that the inla binary was built from an earlier revision than the package, and normally that no changes to that code have been made in the versions in between.

Finn
